description: Operational view of the keeper. Rows are grouped by the question an on-call would ask; each panel answers a slice of it.

panels.title: Running build
panels.description: Version and git commit currently running (keeper_build_info). Line up metric shifts against deploys.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: time() - keeper_start_time_seconds. Drops to ~0 on every restart / redeploy.

panels.title: Tx confirm rate (15m)
panels.description: confirmed ÷ submitted over 15m — the core execution SLI. `KeeperTxConfirmationRateLow` pages below 50%; green ≥90%. Shows 'No data' when nothing is being submitted (idle, not a failure).

panels.title: Profit capture (1h)
panels.description: realised ÷ expected net profit over 1h — the realisation-tax SLI. 100% = every modelled dollar landed on-chain. 'No data' when no plans dispatched.

panels.title: Scan freshness (worst)
panels.description: Oldest 'last successful scan' across all markets. `KeeperScanStalled` fires at 300s. Green ≤60s.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Grafana-managed alert rules currently firing, pending, or in error. Empty = all clear. Rules live in deploy/grafana/provisioning/alerting/.

panels.title: Keeper reachable
panels.description: Green = Prometheus can reach the keeper's `/metrics` endpoint. Red = the keeper is unreachable. Pair with *Time since last successful scan* to tell 'down' from 'up but idle'.

panels.title: Time since last successful scan
panels.description: How long since each market completed a scan. Green ≤30s, yellow ≤60s, red beyond. Shows 'No data' until the first scan lands — pair with *Keeper reachable* to tell 'starting up' from 'stuck'.

panels.title: Plans dispatched (1h)
panels.description: Liquidation plans the keeper decided to act on in the last hour. Red 0 = nothing was liquidatable or the strategy is stuck; correlate with *Skip reasons*.

panels.title: TXs confirmed (1h)
panels.description: Liquidations confirmed on-chain in the last hour. The bot is doing real-money work iff this is non-zero. If *Plans dispatched* is non-zero but this is 0, see *TX confirmation outcomes*.

panels.title: XLM funding
panels.description: Keeper's XLM wallet balance. XLM pays inclusion fees — once it falls below `xlm_safety_margin` the bot stops submitting. See *XLM balance vs safety margin* for the headroom curve.

panels.title: Liquidation pipeline — plans → submitted → confirmed
panels.description: Steady-state: all three series track each other. Plans > submitted = simulations rejecting in the executor. Submitted > confirmed = submissions not landing — see *TX confirmation outcomes* for the breakdown.

panels.title: Scan outcomes
panels.description: Per-scan verdict mix. `ok` should dominate; `no_obligations` is expected on quiet markets; sustained `no_market_data` means the data feed is broken.

panels.title: Obligations vs liquidatable positions
panels.description: Borrowers being modelled vs the subset flagged liquidatable, per market. Sustained zero liquidatable against non-zero obligations is suspicious — usually engine or oracle drift.

panels.title: Skip reasons
panels.description: Why the strategy declined to act on an opportunity. A reason spiking 10× over baseline is the early signal worth investigating.

panels.title: Simulation outcomes
panels.description: Outcome of each simulated contract call. Growing `not_liquidatable` means engine/contract drift; growing `error` means RPC trouble.

panels.title: TX submission outcomes
panels.description: Outcome of each transaction submission attempt. Sustained `retry_exhausted` or `sim_empty` is a red flag.

panels.title: TX confirmation outcomes
panels.description: Outcome of each submitted transaction once we wait for confirmation. `failed_on_chain` is the realisation-tax tail — tx landed but reverted, gas spent. `submission_timeout` is uncertainty (tx may yet land). `transport_error` / `unexpected_status` indicate an RPC regression.

panels.title: Wallet balances per asset
panels.description: On-chain balances per asset held by the keeper. Zero balances block `Own` and `PreSwap` execution modes and stop the rebalancer at dust.

panels.title: Keeper self-position per market
panels.description: What the keeper itself holds in each market — supply (jTokens), borrow (dTokens), plain collateral. The withdrawer operates on supply; non-zero borrow means the keeper is exposed to liquidation itself.

panels.title: XLM balance vs safety margin
panels.description: Live XLM balance against the configured `xlm_safety_margin` floor. Below the floor the keeper refuses to spend XLM to preserve inclusion-fee headroom. Refill when the green line approaches the red dashed line.

panels.title: Is the bot keeping up with the chain?
Dropped events (back-pressure)
panels.description: Any non-zero rate means events are being dropped because a downstream consumer can't keep up. Always urgent — investigate immediately.

panels.title: State persistence & sequence retries
panels.description: `cursor save fail` = the keeper can't write to SQLite, so events would replay after a restart. `bad_seq retries` = Stellar sequence-number contention; sustained values mean another process is using the same signing key.

panels.title: Market scan latency
panels.description: Wall-clock time to evaluate one market end-to-end, split by outcome. Sustained p95 above ~1s usually means RPC roundtrips are slow; flat-but-rising p50 means more obligations are being modelled. `KeeperScanSlow` fires at 5s.

panels.title: RPC simulate latency by function (p95)
panels.description: Per-function p95 of `simulate_transaction` roundtrips. Drill-down for *Market scan latency* — tells you which contract call is the slow one. Outcomes split `ok` from `transport_error` so failed RPCs don't dilute the latency signal.

panels.title: RPC simulate failures by function
panels.description: Per-function rate of failing simulate calls. `transport` = network or RPC-server error (switch providers); `sim_error` = the simulator returned a structured contract error (bad inputs).

panels.title: Expected profit per plan
panels.description: Distribution of modelled profit on each dispatched liquidation plan, per market. This is the dispatch-time profit, not the realised on-chain amount. p50 collapse means we're scraping dust — re-tune `min_profit_margin_cents`.

panels.title: Expected vs realised profit
panels.description: Hourly run-rate of profit on dispatched plans. `expected` totals at dispatch; `realised` totals only when the tx is confirmed on-chain. The gap is the realisation tax — submission failures, simulation drift, retries exhausted. Both lines remain modelled (use `plan.net_profit_oracle`, not seized amounts).

panels.title: Rebalancer outcomes
panels.description: What the rebalancer decided per candidate. `dispatched` is the only success outcome. `nothing_to_swap` is normal; `precondition_*` means config; `evaluation_error` / `reservation_lost` mean trouble. A silent panel means the rebalancer isn't being invoked — check the soroban-event topic filter or `refresh_interval_blocks`.

panels.title: Rebalancer swap size (p50 / p95)
panels.description: USD value of swaps actually emitted. The floor is `rebalancer_min_swap_amount_value_cents`; p50 hugging the floor means dust-only activity — re-tune the threshold.

panels.title: Withdrawer outcomes
panels.description: What the withdrawer decided per position. `dispatched` = action emitted. `pool_at_capacity` / `below_threshold` / `empty_position` are normal pauses. `no_market_data` / `pool_missing` / `build_error` are red flags.

panels.title: Bad-debt initiator outcomes
panels.description: What the bad-debt initiator decided per Liquidate event. `ineligible` is the steady state (most liquidations leave healthy residual collateral). `dispatched` fires only when a borrower is underwater. `parse_error` / `decode_op_error` / `build_failed` mean the strategy can't even evaluate — chase via logs.

title: Alula Liquidator
